results.title: Four killed, three injured in separate road accidents in Australia's New South Wales
results.description: Sydney: Four people have died and three others have been hospitalised with serious injuries following two separate car crashes in the eastern Australian state of New South Wales (NSW). The NSW police force said on Sunday that the first accident occurred shortly before 7 pm (local time) on Saturday when two vehicles collided in the small town of Avoca, 100 km southwest of Sydney. Both occupants of one of the vehicles, who have not been identified, died at the scene, Xinhua News Agency reported. The 64-year-old female driver of the second vehicle and her passenger, a 65-year-old man, were treated at the scene by ambulance paramedics and taken to hospital with serious injuries. Hours later, emergency services in NSW's far north were at 10:30 pm called to reports of a single-vehicle crash near the border with neighbouring Queensland and arrived to find a vehicle had left the road and struck a tree. Two occupants, both believed to be aged in their 20s, were assisted by police before the arrival of ambulance crews, but died at the scene. A third occupant, also aged in 20s, was taken to a Queensland hospital in a serious but stable condition. Police established crime scenes at both crash sites and have commenced investigations. On November 9, a man died and a woman was hospitalised with serious injuries after being struck by a car that crashed into a medical center in the Australian state of Queensland. Queensland Police Service Chief Inspector Grant Marcus told reporters that a vehicle crashed into a medical centre in the city of Bundaberg, about 300 km north of Brisbane, shortly after 10 am (local time) on November 9, striking several people inside. A 63-year-old man, who was in the waiting room when the vehicle crashed, sustained critical injuries and was declared dead a short time later, Xinhua News Agency reported. His partner, a 63-year-old woman, was transported to hospital with life-threatening injuries. Marcus said investigators were working to determine whether speed or a mechanical fault played a role in the crash, but that the incident did not appear to be deliberate. He said the 71-year-old female driver had been taken to hospital with injuries that were not considered serious.

results.title: Auction of $180 million Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
results.description: Auction house Sotheby's says it is working to resolve a dispute over the intended sale of a painting by Vincent van Gogh. Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom"), which carries an estimated value of $180m (£136m), is due to go under the hammer in New York on Wednesday. But representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - say it may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis. Sotheby's says its own "extensive research" has not established this, but that it will work with the family to try and reach a solution. "Sotheby's takes provenance and restitution matters extremely seriously and has undertaken extensive research into the ownership history of Châtaigniers en fleurs," the auction house told the BBC in a statement. "We are aware of the concerns recently raised by representatives of the Fischer heirs and have been in dialogue with them regarding the painting's history. "While our research to date has not established that the painting was sold under duress, we recognise the importance of engaging thoughtfully and constructively with the family and are committed to working toward a mutually satisfactory resolution." The painting is being sold as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection. Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890. It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934. The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotherby's says. Four other owners have had it prior to it being put up for auction this year. Fischer family heirs have instructed a lawyer who, according to the New York Times, has written to Sotherby's on their behalf. He is said to have told the auction house the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment. results.title: Maize Prices Surge 55% In Tamil Nadu's Namakkal, Poultry Farmers Struggle As Egg Production Costs Rise
results.description: Poultry farmers in Tamil Nadu's Namakkal are struggling as maize prices have surged nearly 55%, rising from ₹22 to ₹34 per kg. Inadequate rainfall and reduced supplies from major cultivation areas have triggered shortages. With maize accounting for over 40% of poultry feed, rising procurement costs are significantly increasing egg production expenses across the region.
